_comment: Registration for scripts/eli5-vendor.py (issues #591, #1012).
WHY THIS GATE NEEDS A COMMITTED CASE (ADR 0008): it is a gate that lets
work THROUGH. The CI `eli5-vendor-check` step reads its green as 'the
vendored core is still what cooneycw/eli5-gate published', and nothing
downstream re-derives that fact. A blind version prints the identical
clean line while the core diverges - which is the pre-#591 state, where
the drift script existed and was invoked by no step, no target and no
test.
WHY IT COULD NOT BE REGISTERED BEFORE #1012: the manifest path and the
repository root were module-level constants, so the gate could only ever
read THIS repository. There was no way to aim it at a known-bad tree, so
its green had never been shown to be falsifiable at all. `--root` is what
changed that, which is why the control lands with the refactor.
THE CASES ARE MINIATURE REPOS, not the real one: a tiny document with a
marker pair and a manifest pinning its core. Deliberately small - the
question is whether the gate can tell a pinned core from an edited one,
not whether it can hash 187 real lines. The fixture document also
MENTIONS a marker mid-line in prose, because the real eli5.md does and
line-start anchoring is the rule most likely to break silently.
Stdlib-only, network-free and git-free, like the gate: the fixture
manifest points at example.invalid, so a runner with connectivity and one
without give the same verdict.
detect_signal: ^DRIFT: .* does not match the manifest pin\.$
limits: Covers the OFFLINE half only - the manifest pin. The advisory `--upstream` half (ADR 0008 row 35) fetches the canonical copy and is deliberately fail-open, so a case cannot be committed for it without a network; its fail-open behaviour is asserted in tests/test_eli5_vendor.py instead. This control also says nothing about whether the REAL vendored core is correct - that is the gate's own run in CI, over the real tree.

cases.name: bad-drifted-core
cases.why: One sentence of the marker-delimited core edited in place, markers intact and the manifest pin untouched - the exact shape of someone fixing the gate text in CPP instead of in cooneycw/eli5-gate. If this scores GOOD the gate cannot see a local edit at all, which is the only thing the offline half exists to see.

cases.name: good-pinned-core
cases.why: The same tree with the core matching its pin. THE HALF THAT MATTERS for a gate wedged at 'fail': a check that refuses every tree is indistinguishable from a working one on the bad case alone, and would redden CI until someone deleted the step.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED, not historical: the pre-#1012 gate hardcoded its repository root, so pointed at a case it would have read the real repository and answered a different question rather than answering this one blindly - which disqualifies it as an anchor. This is the plausible weaker check written instead: confirm the document is present and still carries its marker pair, and call that vendored. It catches a deleted file or a broken marker pair, and is blind to the failure that actually happens - a core edited in place. It MISSES the known-bad input and AGREES with the current gate on the known-good one.
